text.p: Bear Stearns said it maintains its attractive rating on Brazilian telecoms holging Telebras following release of second-quarter 1997 results.
-- "Earnings were within the range we were expecting, but were below the first call consensus of $2.53 per ADR, Bear Stearns analysts Rizwan Ali, C.A. Recouso and daniel Parker said in a report.
-- The company on Friday reported earnings of $746 million, or $2.33 per ADR, for the second quarter compared with $692 million or $2.16 per ADR in the same period last year, they said.

-- The analysts said that, with first half earnings of $1.5 billion, or $4.33 per ADR, the firm was in line to meet their estimates of $9.70 per ADR for 1997 though their forecast is below the $10.40 market consensus.
-- "Based on our somewhat conservative valuation, Telebras still offers a reasonable upside to $170 in the next 12 to 18 months," they added.

-- Second quarter revenues rose 24 percent from the same period last year, while the firm improved operating and EBITDA margins to 35 percent and 61 percent versus 33 percent and 60 percent a year ago, they said.
-- The results also were helped by a tariff restructuring that lower long-distance tariffs, but raised local call rates starting May 19, they said.
-- The full impact of the restructuring should be felt in the third quarter.
-- Telebras' ADR closed down 3/11 at 136-1/2 in New York, while its preferred share ended off 2.63 percent at 148 reais and its common fell 2.87 percent to close off 135.50 reais in Sao Paulo.
